newsitem.title: ISRAEL: ILDC to double hotel rooms by year end.
newsitem.headline: ILDC to double hotel rooms by year end.

text.p: Israel Land Development Co (ILDC) plans to double the number of hotel rooms it manages under the Howard Johnson name to 1,200 by the end of the year, the company said on Tuesday.

Managing Director Ofer Nimrodi said at a ribbon cutting ceremony marking the opening of ILDC's first four Howard Johnson hotels that part of the proceeds from a 130 million shekel ($38 million) public offering ILDC is making next week in Tel Aviv would be used to finance the expansion.
ILDC said said it hoped to expand by the end of 1998 to 2,500 rooms, which would make it a leading player in the Israeli hotel sector.

The company said it was in talks with a number of hotels in the centre of the country to bring them into the Howard Johnson's network and is building a 17-storey hotel in Jerusalem due for completion by the end of 1998.

ILDC, through its publicly traded Hachsharat Hayishuv Hotels subsidiary, owns and manages four hotels with atotal of 600 rooms -- two in Israel's southern resort of Eilat, and one each in the northern towns of Tiberias and Safed.

ILDC said it was also in advanced negotiations with the Palestinian Authority about managing hotels in the autonomous areas. The company said it was in talks with hotels in Greece, Turkey and Cyprus where ILDC holds the Howard Johnson franchise as well.

Howard Johnson is controlled by HFS Inc, which also controls the Days Inn, Travel Lodge and Ramada franshises. Days Inn operates in Israel under a separate franchise agreement. HFS signed a master franchise agreement with ILDC for Howard Johnson in April.
